overall: The tables support a null pooled effect on accuracy (1.0 point, CI [-0.3, 2.4]) and three nominal arm-level H1 effects with p between 0.004 and 0.043. They do not support treating those effects as robust. With 44 uncorrected tests, the exclusion rerun (H1a) removes two of the three effects, and the Guide's interval barely clears zero. The most important caveat is that only Automated Flagging survives the low-knowledge exclusion, and then only at p=0.044. The E1 and E2 findings are unsupported because their tables are empty.

issues.issue: The tables have empty estimate columns, yet the Finding lines claim effects were eliminated (E1) and that effects are not concentrated in either familiarity group and 'likely reflect sampling variability' (E2). The review flagged these claims as unsupported but the text still carries them. E1 is also still labelled 'attention-check failures', although pk_score<1 is a knowledge screen.
issues.fix: Populate the tables with estimates, SEs and an arm-by-familiarity interaction test, or delete the conclusions. Relabel E1 as a low-knowledge exclusion.
issues.disposition_reason: The E1 and E2 tables are empty, so the conclusions must be deleted or the tables populated, and E1 needs relabelling as a low-knowledge exclusion.

issues.issue: H1a (dropping 613 low-knowledge respondents) shows Mindfulness becoming non-significant (p=0.12) and the Guide shrinking to 0.023 (p=0.39). Only Automated Flagging survives, at p=0.044. The H1a section has no prose, and the abstract and Key findings present all three H1 effects without this caveat. Excluding on pk_score could also be post-treatment if it was measured after treatment.
issues.fix: Add H1a prose and report that two of the three effects are not robust to the exclusion. Clarify when pk_score was measured.
issues.disposition_reason: The H1a estimates already exist, so the fix is prose that reports the non-robustness and when pk_score was measured.

issues.issue: The three H1 effects are labelled 'Registered' and described as raising or lowering accuracy, but there are 44 uncorrected tests and p-values of 0.032 to 0.043. The Guide's CI lower bound is 0.2 points. The wording is too strong.
issues.fix: Report Holm/BH-adjusted p-values beside the registered ones as a supplementary robustness check, and describe the effects as nominal.
issues.disposition_reason: The plan specifies no multiple-testing correction, so adjusted p-values would change the registered analysis. The wording can be softened to 'nominal' without it.

issues.issue: The prose calls the pooled -0.11 a result and says 'one arm out of eleven could arise by chance'. The Breathing SE (0.23) is far larger than most other arms' SEs, which the review flagged. Pooled I² is 0 even though SEs vary widely. The unadjusted H2a Breathing estimate (-0.63) is also not discussed.
issues.fix: Report H2a in the text, run leverage and outlier diagnostics for the Lin interaction model, and soften the interpretation.
issues.disposition_reason: Leverage and outlier diagnostics on the Lin model can be run on the same data, and H2a can be discussed in the text.

issues.issue: IPW construction, exclusion rules and attrition by arm are not reported (227 respondents dropped). Control n=181 is much smaller than most treatment arms. Part of the data pre-dated registration, but it is not stated which arms or batches.

rounds.overall: The registered H1 tables support small gains for Automated Flagging (+4.4 points) and the AI Literacy Guide (+4.7 points) and a loss for Mindfulness (-3.9 points). All three are nominal, with p between 0.004 and 0.043, and the plan specifies no multiplicity correction across 44 tests. The pooled effect on accuracy is not distinguishable from zero. The other outcomes show scattered effects. The most important caveat is that the exploratory E1 and E2 tables are empty, so their conclusions (effects vanish when low-knowledge respondents are dropped; effects reflect sampling variability) cannot be checked and should not be reported. The 'one-sided' label in Key findings contradicts the two-sided tables.

issues.issue: The E1 table has empty est/se/p columns for every arm, yet the text claims that Automated Flagging (p=0.004) and AI Literacy Guide (p=0.043) became nonsignificant. Nothing displayed supports this. The 'attention-check failure' label is also misleading: pk_score<1 is a knowledge-question failure, not an attention check, and may be post-treatment-correlated or confounded with ability. Dropping 30% of the sample is not a clean robustness test.

The E2 table is empty, so the 'no arm reached p<0.05' claim cannot be checked. Concluding that the effects 'likely reflect sampling variability' from underpowered subgroups (n=25 to 219) is overreach. No interaction test is reported.

The 'pooled' estimate is described as 'accuracy 1.0 point higher', and the Key findings headline says 'Registered: ...p=0.004, one-sided', but the tables say two-sided. The 44 tests have no multiplicity correction. The 'registered' label is applied to effects that would not survive correction (Holm/BH), and the registration content (directional vs two-sided, correction plan) is not shown.

The text says the other ten arms had estimates 'between −0.16 and 0.00', but the pooled random-effects result (−0.11, p=0.026) is reported as significant and tied to nothing in the narrative. The Breathing Exercise result (−0.54) has an SE of 0.23 that is much larger than the other arms' SEs, and arm-level SEs vary oddly (0.116 to 0.280), which suggests the Lin interaction model or outliers are driving them.

The H5 narrative is missing. Pooled p is shown as 'p = 0.000', and the significant AI Accuracy Nudge, Breathing, and Literacy Guide effects are not described. The exploratory H5/H6 contrast (detecting fakes improves while real-content accuracy does not) suggests a shift in response bias rather than discernment, but no discernment measure is given.

The text says 'all p>0.116, max p=0.816', which is garbled (min p=0.116). A placebo on pk_score, which may be measured after treatment, is not clearly a pre-treatment check. 'Confirming the randomisation' is too strong.

Some data existed at registration, and the registration amended an earlier one (#151208). Attrition (227 dropped) is not explained, and the exclusion criteria are not given. IPW weights are used, but their construction is not described. Arm sizes are very unequal (control n=181).

The retrieved list includes irrelevant items (chronic kidney disease, PRISMA-P, mortality risk), and the claim that Capraro et al. 'frame generative AI as a vector for misinformation' is not clearly supported by that paper (it concerns socioeconomic inequalities).
Overstated claim: "AI Literacy Guide by 4.7 points (95% CI [0.2, 9.2])". H1 table: 0.047, CI [0.002, 0.092], p=0.043. The interval almost reaches zero and the test is uncorrected.
Overstated claim: "Pooled across arms, accuracy was 1.0 point higher (95% CI [−0.3, 2.4])". Pooled estimate 0.010, SE 0.007, p=0.132. The interval includes zero.
Unsupported claim: "Automated Flagging ... p=0.004, one-sided". The H1 table states two-sided tests, and p_directional equals the two-sided p.

Unsupported claim: "dropping attention-check failures reportedly removed the two accuracy gains". The E1 table has empty est/se/p columns. pk_score<1 is a knowledge-question failure, not an attention check.
Unsupported claim: "No arm reached p<0.05 ... effects likely reflect sampling variability". The E2 table is empty and no interaction test is reported. Subgroups are small.

Overstated claim: "No intervention significantly affected pre-treatment knowledge (all p > 0.116, max p = 0.816), confirming the randomisation". E3 table: min p=0.116, max p=0.816. A null on 11 arm-level tests does not confirm randomisation, and the timing of pk_score is unclear.
